scope: Five newly imported October-December 2024 packets. Historical findings; no claim of present project status or full attachment audit.

findings.title: Pennsylvania design agreement: new scope and remaining authority
findings.summary: Council awarded IDC an amended and restated agreement not to exceed $1,884,482. The staff report separates $1,209,191 of additional scope from $675,291 remaining on the prior contract; the cumulative agreement history totals $3,134,124. These are different accounting measures, not three new awards.
findings.limit: The report targeted Ready to List in September 2025 and reported bridge design at 60%, track at 25% and civil at 50%. These are October 2024 statements, not verified current progress or a construction start. Executed agreement, later schedule and payments remain separate checks.

findings.title: Pennsylvania environmental agreement has conflicting amounts
findings.status: Approved in the combined J.2/J.3 motion
findings.summary: The minutes and recommended action specify $86,698 for Moffatt & Nichol. The staff report fiscal section instead states $86,989 and says no additional funds were requested. The report describes NEPA technical studies as 80% complete, with permitting to follow approval.
findings.limit: The $291 difference remains unresolved; do not silently substitute one amount for the other or count the restated balance as entirely new spending. Obtain the executed agreement and payment ledger. The reported study percentage is dated October 2024.

findings.title: Development impact fees were continued on October 1
findings.summary: Council continued the development impact fee nexus study and fee schedule to November 5, 2024. The published recommendation to adopt maximum justified fees, with storm-drain fees at 50%, was not adopted at this meeting.
findings.limit: The December 3 staff report later describes a November 5 study approval. Check that later decision and adopted schedule before stating effective fees; this October item establishes only the continuance.

findings.title: Banning and Calimesa truck-route coordination
findings.summary: Council confirmed Lara and Voigt as representatives and directed staff to contact Banning and Calimesa for a 2x2x2 ad hoc meeting on truck routes.
findings.limit: This establishes coordination authority, not a new truck-route ordinance, road standard or intercity agreement.

findings.title: Job creation and retention incentive program authorized
findings.summary: Council authorized the City Manager to develop and implement the Job Creation and Retention Incentive Program.
findings.limit: This does not establish individual business awards, disbursements, job counts or compliance with incentive conditions. Those require executed agreements and performance records.

findings.title: City-owned property discussion received
findings.summary: The minutes record a presentation about City-owned properties and their use.
findings.limit: No sale, lease, redevelopment award or approved property-use decision is recorded under this item. Check later public actions before describing an agreement.

findings.title: Pennsylvania budget increased with SB 125 funding
findings.status: CIP amendment and Attachment E approved unanimously
findings.summary: The approved second FY2025-2029 CIP amendment includes a $5 million SB 125 grant increase for Pennsylvania grade separation, taking its project budget from $8,678,556 to $13,678,556. This follows the lower budget in the October 1 reports.
findings.limit: The increase updates the budget snapshot; it is not evidence of cash received, full construction funding or a revised total project estimate. Reconcile with grant terms and subsequent CIP changes.

findings.title: Police station design and construction combined in PS-07
findings.summary: The amendment closes PS-09 and combines it with PS-07. The staff report shows $3,597,372 existing budget, $3,865,000 in General Fund additions and a $1 million PS-09 transfer, yielding $8,462,372 for PS-07.
findings.limit: The transfer is not an additional $1 million on top of the stated new budget. This is a historical budget reorganization, not a final station cost, construction award or completion finding.

findings.title: CIP amendment adds streetlights, signals and park funding
findings.summary: The amendment includes a $112,000 LED streetlight project, three future-location traffic signals at $600,000 each and a $2 million citywide signal-system upgrade. P-20 playgrounds with shade increases from $250,000 to $290,000; Sports Park lighting increases from $350,000 to $410,000.
findings.limit: The report calls the signal locations tentative. These are dated CIP budgets, not completed installations. Citywide playground and Sports Park allocations do not establish a Stewart Park-specific award.

findings.title: IA 17D special-tax bond issuance authorized
findings.summary: Council authorized Improvement Area 17D Series 2024 special-tax bonds up to $10.5 million. The minutes describe approximately $9.4 million par and a final maturity of September 1, 2054.
findings.limit: The authorization ceiling and anticipated par are distinct. Confirm closing documents for actual issuance, proceeds, rates and debt service; the resolution is not evidence of expenditure.

findings.title: Requisition 2 for $8.25 million approved
findings.summary: Council authorized the City Manager to sign Requisition 2 for release of $8,250,000 in 2016-3 bond proceeds to reimburse Tri Pointe project costs under the February 7, 2017 settlement.
findings.limit: Approval to request trustee disbursement does not itself establish the payment date, bank transfer or final cost eligibility.

findings.title: Mesa Lift Station construction and support awards
findings.summary: Council awarded Borden construction authority of $6,805,797 plus $680,580 in change orders, capped at $7,486,377. Separate awards were $17,510 for Converse materials testing and $92,275 for Webb engineering support.
findings.limit: The construction ceiling already includes its contingency. The testing and engineering awards are separate; authorization does not establish actual expenditure or project completion.

findings.title: WRCOG Fellowship Program participation
findings.summary: Council approved participation in the FY2024-25 WRCOG Fellowship Program and authorized agreements subject to legal review with non-substantive changes.
findings.limit: This is a program participation action, not a WRCOG settlement, restitution receipt or debt payment. No change to the restitution balance is inferred.

findings.title: First-quarter budget amendments approved
findings.summary: Council received the September 30, 2024 financial-status report and approved attached amendments. The staff report states additional spending authority of $158,394 General Fund, $6,300 PEG Fund and $14,999 Other Special Revenue Fund.
findings.limit: Spending authority is not actual expenditure. The staff report identifies the $14,999 as moved from the General Fund, so interfund changes should not be added as wholly independent net City spending.

findings.title: Cash, investments and pension funding reports received
findings.summary: Council received the first-quarter cash and investment report and CalPERS funding update. The pension staff report cites preliminary CalPERS investment returns of 9.3% and an estimated funded status of 79%.
findings.limit: Those figures are attributed estimates in the pension update, not a verified Beaumont plan-specific funded ratio or a new pension appropriation. Read the actuarial and GovInvest records for plan-specific liabilities.

findings.title: Police manager and technical-unit benefit side letters
findings.summary: Council authorized Side Letter 4 increasing the cafeteria plan for Police Managers and the Manager Professional Technical Unit.
findings.limit: The authorization does not establish additional sworn staffing, deployment, realized benefit costs or delivery of service. Executed side letters and payroll records are separate evidence.

findings.title: 960 Beaumont Avenue facade agreement revised
findings.summary: The revised ED2023-0004 agreement supports two phases. The staff report states a maximum City reimbursement of $40,242.35: $19,418.85 after Phase One and $20,823.50 after Phase Two, against $80,484.69 in project costs.
findings.limit: The program reimburses eligible completed work. Agreement approval is not proof of either phase being completed or reimbursed; collect inspections, reimbursement requests and payments.

findings.title: CDBG applications authorized with adjustable funding
findings.summary: Council authorized a $128,350 pedestrian-project application, $10,000 for Voices for Children and the remaining available funding for Boys & Girls Club, subject to CDBG conditions. The City Manager could adjust project funding to the final available allocation.
findings.limit: These are application authorizations, not final grant awards or expenditures. Preserve the final-allocation condition when comparing later funding agreements.

findings.title: Director position changes and budget adjustments
findings.summary: Council approved $31,157 for department 1350, addition of an Economic Development Director, and $147,185 for department 1235.
findings.limit: This establishes position and budget authority. Hiring, executed employment terms and actual compensation require subsequent records.

findings.title: 6.26-acre donation agreement authorized
findings.summary: Council authorized a donation agreement with Lassen Development Partners for 6.26 acres identified as APN 424-010-007.
findings.limit: The motion authorizes an agreement; it does not prove recorded conveyance, accepted title or a future development approval. No PLUS policy amendment is inferred.

findings.title: Permit tracking: communication improvements directed
findings.summary: The minutes record direction to implement communication aspects of planning-project and building-permit tracking.
findings.limit: The record does not establish that a new tracking system was delivered or that processing times improved. Collect implementation records and measured results; this did not amend PLUS.

findings.title: Financial, development-fee and sponsorship policies presented
findings.status: Consent motion recorded; result not stated
findings.summary: The packet seeks approval of GASB 87/96 accounting policies, a financial-management update and a sponsorship/donation policy. The financial-management staff report proposes a development-impact-fee study every five years and cites a November 5, 2024 study approval.
findings.limit: The collected December 3 minutes record a consent motion and list these actions, but omit an explicit carried result or vote tally. Confirm adopted policies and resolutions before treating the packet drafts as executed policy or current requirements.

findings.title: FY2024-25 CDBG supplemental agreement
findings.status: Consent motion recorded; result not stated
findings.summary: The collected minutes list the supplemental agreement supporting Pedestrian Sidewalk Safety Improvement Project Phase II and local nonprofit activities, with authority requested for City Manager execution.
findings.limit: The minutes omit an explicit consent-motion result. Collect the executed supplemental agreement and funding allocations; this prior-year program is separate from the November applications for FY2025-26.

findings.title: Truck-route road viability report received
findings.summary: Council received the report on existing roads along designated truck routes.
findings.limit: Receipt of a road-condition analysis is not adoption of revised truck routes, a road-strength guarantee or a construction award. Later design, funding and route actions require their own records.

findings.title: Potrero benefit-area planning: studies before funding decisions
findings.summary: Staff described a Fehr & Peers focused nexus and infrastructure-delivery study and a sewer study being advertised, to coordinate roads, sewers and lift stations serving future development. Future facility-funding options were to return to Council.
findings.limit: This item did not approve the listed developments, annexations, a final benefit-area fee or construction funding. Keep this extension-area planning separate from interchange Phase II delivery.

findings.title: Fourth Street/Potrero indemnification agreement
findings.summary: Council authorized the Mayor to execute an indemnification agreement with Riverside County for right-of-way dedications near Potrero Boulevard and Fourth Street.
findings.limit: The authorization is not proof of agreement execution, recorded dedications, construction commencement or interchange completion.

findings.title: IA 17D reimbursement approvals kept separate
findings.summary: Council approved Requisition 003 for $8,863,651.89 and a separate $214,799.45 PayGo request for TUMF fees. The minutes break the requisition into $7,452,415.96 of improvements and $1,411,235.93 of development impact fees.
findings.limit: The two requests use different funding streams. Do not count their components twice or infer trustee disbursement, City cash receipt or a WRCOG restitution credit from these approvals.

findings.title: Tract 32850 plot-plan item removed
findings.summary: The minutes state that the applicant rescinded the application and item I.2 was removed without discussion. This differs from the published recommendation to continue it to December 17.
findings.limit: This meeting does not establish approval of the proposed 95 residential lots and park site.

findings.title: FY2024 financial reports and audit sources
findings.status: Consent motion recorded; result not stated
findings.summary: The packet includes the Popular Annual Financial Report, ACFR and internal-control report. The staff report describes an unmodified financial-statement opinion and no significant deficiencies or material weaknesses identified in the audit.
findings.limit: These statements are attributed to the staff report; a clean financial-statement opinion does not certify every transaction or service result. The collected minutes omit an explicit consent-motion result. Use the audit attachments for the underlying opinions and scope.

findings.title: FY2025-26 budget development timeline
findings.summary: The December packet supplies the proposed FY2025-26 budget calendar for review and direction.
findings.limit: This is a process calendar, not adoption of the FY2025-26 budget. The minutes omit an explicit consent-motion result; later hearings and adopted budget documents establish final authority.

findings.title: TUMF ordinance and fee-schedule action
findings.summary: Council approved the motion addressing the ordinance updating TUMF participation and the resolution amending applicable TUMF fees. The staff report ties the proposal to WRCOG's 2024 nexus study.
findings.limit: The minutes do not establish the later second-reading record or every fee's effective date. Collect final instruments and subsequent action before applying the packet schedule as current law. This is not evidence of a settlement payoff or restitution receipt.

findings.title: Welcome to Beaumont billboard relocation approved
findings.summary: Council approved PLAN2024-0108 to relocate and replace the Welcome to Beaumont electronic billboard at 1691 East Sixth Street.
findings.limit: Permit approval is not evidence of installation, advertising revenue, contract execution or a completed replacement.

findings.title: Grace Avenue and Sixth Street condition assessments
findings.summary: Council awarded one-year IMEG facility-condition assessment agreements for 500 Grace Avenue and 105 Sixth Street. The staff report lists fixed fees of $54,894 and $40,776, respectively, funded from CD-03.
findings.limit: These fund assessments of conditions and potential food/beverage use upgrades, not a construction award, tenant lease or completed redevelopment. Collect executed agreements and assessment deliverables.

findings.title: Wastewater SCADA integration services
findings.summary: Council awarded SKM Engineering SCADA programming and wastewater system-integration services not to exceed $75,000.
findings.limit: The service award does not establish commissioning, cybersecurity outcomes, final payment or facility completion.

findings.title: Second Street Extension federal grant agreement
findings.summary: Council approved HUD grant agreement B-24-CP-CA-0317 and execution authority. The minutes identify $1 million of federal Community Project Funding for the Second Street Extension.
findings.limit: This is the same $1 million funding source included in the October 15 CIP amendment, not an additional grant to add again. Grant execution, reimbursement and construction completion remain separate checks.
